terms.meaning: Declining to supply an answer when sufficient evidence is unavailable.
The fraction of evaluated examples counted as correct.
Small added weights trained while the base is fixed.
An interface through which one program asks another to do work.
A numbered position used to select an item or a matrix row.
Automatic speech recognition: turning speech audio into text.
One set of query, key and value projections and its weighted information mixture.
Generate a next token from the input and previously generated tokens.
Processing several inputs together in one model operation.
Two neighbouring symbols; this model predicts from the previous character only.
Predicting between two labels, here real and generated.
A keyword-ranking method based on term matches and their frequency.
Stored results reused when an equivalent request returns.
A model predicting the next token from the tokens already present.
A rule preventing a position from attending to later positions.
Model-specific formatting used to represent roles and messages as a token sequence.
A passage cut from a document for indexing and retrieval.
A similarity between image and text representations; it is not a complete quality measure.
The probability of an outcome when some other information is already given.
The input text made available to a language model for a response.
A comparison of vector directions, independent of vector length.
A network that turns a representation or previous outputs into predictions for the output.
The learned network; here it predicts added noise from noisy data and a timestep.
Rank passages by similarity between learned question and passage vectors.
Keep tensor values while disconnecting their gradient path for an operation.
Generation through learned denoising of a noisy representation.
A network trained to distinguish dataset examples from generated examples.
An image-to-image setting controlling how much the input is perturbed before denoising.
A lower bound on data log-likelihood; its negative balances reconstruction and KL at beta = 1.
A numerical vector representing an item, often learned, for prediction or comparison.
A network that converts input data into numerical representations or distribution parameters.
A URL and request handler through which a program exposes an operation.
One pass through the training data.
Code that runs examples, scores outputs and collects comparable measures.
A numerical representation extracted from an intermediate layer of a network.
A small neural network applied separately at each token position.
A prompt containing several examples of the desired input/output behaviour.
A fixed procedure that progressively corrupts clean data with noise.
A model weight held unchanged by the optimizer during training.
A named piece of code taking inputs and returning an output.
Random numerical values drawn from a bell-shaped distribution.
A network that transforms a random code into a generated example.
A measure of how changing a quantity would change a loss.
A training cost encouraging the critic's input-gradient norm to stay near one on sampled interpolates.
A reference answer or observation used to check a model output.
Combining conditional and reference predictions to influence prompt-following during sampling.
Generated content that presents an unsupported or incorrect claim as if it were reliable.
A numerical array holding a batch of images, their channels, rows, and columns.
An instruction planted in retrieved data that tries to redirect the assistant.
Using a trained model to predict or generate without updating its learned weights.
A category describing what a customer's message is asking about.
A structured text format for exchanging fields and values, including objects and lists.
A non-negative measure of how one probability distribution differs from another.
The elapsed time from a request to its result; first-token latency measures the initial wait.
A shorter hidden numerical representation used by the model.
Generating in a compact image representation before a decoder converts it to pixels.
An unnormalised model score. Sigmoid or softmax can turn logits into probabilities.
Code that repeats a task for several items or steps.
Small trainable matrices adding a low-rank correction to selected base-model projections.
A number measuring prediction error during training.
Multiplying a vector by learned weights to produce another vector.
The number of rows and columns in a table of numbers.
A protocol through which applications discover and call tools and access resources.
The centre of a distribution and a measure of its spread.
The average squared difference between predicted and target numbers.
A type of data, such as text, images or audio, with its own structure.
A generator produces only a small part of the variety present in the training distribution.
A learned number used by a neural network to transform its input.
Mean reciprocal rank: average one over each first relevant result's rank; missing results score zero.
A score measuring how surprising observed data is; lower is better for those data.
Learned numbers used to transform an input into a prediction.
Numbers specifying how much signal and noise appear at each timestep.
The generator objective that asks D to label generated samples as real.
The leading token candidates retained by a top-p cumulative-probability threshold.
Learning training examples in a way that fails to improve predictions on separate examples.
A latency value at or below which roughly 95% of measured requests fall.
Two examples marked as describing the same content.
A projection that compresses vectors into fewer dimensions for inspection.
The exponential of average negative log-probability, summarising prediction uncertainty.
A judge's preference for an answer's placement rather than its quality.
The fraction of the k returned results that are relevant.
The chosen code distribution used for generating new examples, here N(0, I).
A number from 0 to 1 describing how likely an outcome is.
Nonnegative probabilities for possible outcomes, adding to one.
A learned mapping connecting feature dimensions or representation spaces.
Instructions and context supplied to a model for one request.
Instructions inside supplied content that attempt to redirect the model's task.
Information about a media item's origin and editing history.
Representing weights with a limited set of values, often to store fewer bits.
Learned vectors used to compare tokens and mix their information.
The adapter's intermediate feature dimension, controlling its correction capacity and parameter count.
A model that reorders candidate passages by reading them with the question.
Learning to predict numerical values rather than selecting a class label.
Writing a random code as learned shift and scale applied to independent noise.
Adding a sublayer's output to the vector entering that sublayer.
Reciprocal rank fusion: combine rankings using candidates' rank positions.
The procedure that uses model predictions to turn starting noise into an output.
Drawing an outcome randomly according to a probability distribution.
A specification of output fields, types and allowed values.
A vector space where corresponding inputs from different modalities can be compared.
A score comparing two representations; larger means more similar here.
Turns a row of scores into nonnegative numbers summing to one.
Learning from supplied input prompts and known desired responses.
A positive divisor on model scores that changes how concentrated sampling probabilities are.
An array whose axes name groups such as batch, token position and feature.
The number of entries along each dimension of an array.
Work completed per unit time, such as total generated tokens per second.
A unit processed or generated by a model; a text token can be a word, word part or character.
An integer identifying a text unit in one particular tokenizer's vocabulary.
A named function application code can run for the model.
A structured request for the program to run a named function.
Separate examples for learning, choosing settings and final measurement.
Learning a model's parameters or probability table from data.
A number used to measure mistakes and guide weight updates.
The known answer used to measure a model's prediction error.
Time to first token; this lab approximates it with first non-empty decoded text.
Text-to-speech: turning written words into an audio waveform.
An image network with shrinking and expanding spatial stages joined by skip connections.
An ordered list of numbers used to represent an item.
A vision-language model that processes images together with text.
Word substitutions, deletions and insertions divided by reference word count.
A prompt describing the task without including worked input/output examples.
Select a class by comparing descriptions, without training on that task's labels.
